title: The Afternoon Brief: Tokenized stocks surge to $3.1B as AMC legal threat looms
dek: Robinhood's tokenized stock platform has scaled to record $3.1 billion in market value while facing its first formal legal challenge from AMC Entertainment. The network's infrastructure halted briefly on Saturday even as institutional capital continues flowing into Bitcoin ETFs.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The tokenized stock market has grown eight-fold in six months to $3.1 billion, but the legal status of issuing stock price tokens without corporate consent remains unresolved; AMC's instruction to counsel and a Robinhood Chain infrastructure failure on the same day signal deepening operational and regulatory stress on the model.
bottom_line: Tokenized stocks hit a record $3.1 billion market cap on Saturday, but the asset class now faces its first formal corporate legal challenge from AMC and a significant infrastructure failure on Robinhood Chain, the largest issuer. The legal status of issuing synthetic stock tokens without corporate consent remains unresolved, and whether corporate objections will reshape the market's operational boundaries is the key checkpoint in the coming weeks. Bitcoin ETF inflows remain robust at $175 million on September 4, though the week-to-date shift from exchange inflows to outflows signals tactical positioning ahead of pending regulatory clarity. The desk will track AMC's counsel findings and Robinhood's public disclosure of the block production cause as material indicators of whether this market can sustain its growth trajectory.
body: Saturday's picture is one of rapid scale meeting sudden friction. Tokenized stocks reached an all-time high of $3.1 billion in combined market capitalization, according to the desk's reporting, with BNB Chain capturing one-third of the market and Robinhood Chain becoming the largest stock token issuer by holder count in roughly two months since its mainnet launch on July 1. Yet on the same day, Robinhood Chain experienced a 14-minute halt in block production, and AMC Entertainment's CEO formally instructed outside securities counsel to investigate whether Robinhood's unregistered stock tokens are legal.

The infrastructure failure is the more immediate technical concern. Robinhood Chain has generated about $23 million in cumulative fees with roughly $4 million collected in a recent 24-hour period, and Token Terminal estimated that the network accounted for 78.5% of layer-2 blockchain revenue over the past 30 days. The cause of Saturday's block production halt has not been publicly disclosed. Robinhood's chief legal officer responded to AMC that the company would not stop issuing the tokens and invited AMC's lawyers to mount a legal challenge.

The legal question cuts deeper. As the desk reported earlier, AMC CEO Adam Aron called the tokens "contemptible, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable, and vile" on September 3, stating that AMC has no connection to them and questioning their legality. Robinhood's stock tokens are structured as tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited, giving token holders economic exposure to a share price but no legal claim on the underlying company. The tokens are not registered under U.S. securities laws and cannot be offered to U.S. persons. Whether a synthetic, offshore-issued product tracking a company's stock constitutes an unregistered security under U.S. law remains unresolved by any court or regulator.

The market has not waited for clarity. On-chain decentralized exchanges generated about $6.4 billion in tokenized stock volume over the past 30 days, up more than 90% from the preceding period, with PancakeSwap and Uniswap dominating at roughly $3.1 billion and $2.5 billion respectively. The market expanded more than eightfold over the past six months to roughly 2.6 million holders across all tokenized-stock platforms.

On the tape, the desk's boards show mixed signals. Bitcoin traded at $79,978 on Saturday, up 0.39% on the day and up 24.79% over the month, with the Fear & Greed Index at 73 (Greed). The desk's Whale Watch board shows $99.6 million in bitcoin moving off exchanges over the past 24 hours, reversing the week-ending-September 5 pattern: the week as a whole saw $494 million in bitcoin move off exchanges, a sharp reversal from the three prior weeks when $2.2 billion moved onto exchanges. Ethereum, up 0.95% on the day but down 1.08% on the week, saw $25.9 million in spot ETF inflows on September 4, though year-to-date Bitcoin ETF inflows of $55.7 billion dwarf Ethereum's $13.2 billion. BNB, the dominant network for tokenized stocks, surged 7.71% on the day and 37.67% over the month, with its RSI at 79.6, suggesting overbought conditions.

The reporting does not explain whether the flow reversal and BNB's strength reflect rotation into tokenized stocks or broader sentiment shifts. Similarly, the cause of the Robinhood Chain outage and its duration beyond 14 minutes are not disclosed.
